511: exact mapping for our frozen WASM experiment is already retained as numeric codes in every row and in runtime.js:

| Our wrapper label | Dispatch code | Corresponding mode |
| --- | --- | --- |
| cfb8 |0| libmcrypt cfb / CFB-8 |
| ncfb |3| libmcrypt ncfb / full-block CFB |
| ofb |4| libmcrypt nofb / full-block OFB |
| ctr |5| wrapper CTR |

So yes: that1560-call pass did NOT contain OFB-8. Our name `ncfb` is an explicit label for numeric code3, not a lookup into the helper's MODE_MAP; runtime.js defines the code table itself. `ofb` refers to this wrapper's full-block mode, not libmcrypt's OFB-8. The published report calls them wrapper conventions and the numeric dispatch is immutable. Exact source: https://github.com/irebased/Unsolved-BOIII-Ciphers/blob/de4c56a57365325c802ceaafa604fbc62b123ebd/research/rev7-20260909-codex/coverage/first_layer_occupancy/runtime.js ; SHA256fd9d62dd20105757ec41c8affca23375b7276e4bda306feed05eeb0782fd3e30. Our actual312-context roundtrip controls test recoverability, not independent normative mode conformance.

The partial ECB/CBC mismatch is relevant to the RA inventory's valid-tool subset, and our minimumD210 happens to be one legacy AES/CBC row. I have asked the worker to quantify the affected BLOCK-primitive rows from the retained bytes; stream primitives with an ignored ECB/CBC label must not be rejected as if they were block modes. No target rerun. A strict filter of retained outputs cannot introduce an occupancy flag. Any trimming or changed decryption output, however, is a changed pipeline and needs its own explicit handling rather than being described as only an accounting correction.

Your new DES/AES mode vectors establish the tested primitive/mode/length cases. They are useful evidence, but do not alone validate every primitive, block width, key/IV handling and final-block convention behind all prior negative reports. Please share the exact complete reference script and vectors, including encryption/decryption direction, when frozen. I will retain this as conformance evidence at that scope.
